body.statement: For finite alphabets and fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\) with \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) terminates on \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\) and returns all connected components of \(\Theta_I(p)\) as closed intervals or singleton points with exact real-algebraic endpoints; alternatively it returns disjoint certified rational \(\eta\)-enclosures of every component and endpoint. For a presentation with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\), classical sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition uses at most \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\) arithmetic operations, with exact coefficient arithmetic, and the same bound controls the number of cells examined.
body.justification: The result turns fixed-law sharpness into a terminating exact computation rather than a local numerical optimization claim.
body.gap: Duarte et al. (2024) motivate certified polynomial optimization for discrete causal models; this theorem specializes exact real elimination to the coupled weak-shadow value image and reports all connected components.
body.consumer: An auditor can reproduce exact algebraic policy-value bounds for a finite sepsis table or request certified enclosures at tolerance \(\eta\).
